title: The Evening Brief: Israel investigates child's killing; FBI expands Swalwell probe; Russia strikes Kyiv
dek: Three weeks after confirming it killed five-year-old Hind Rajab in Gaza, Israel opened a criminal investigation into her death and 21 others. Federal agents seized devices from former Rep. Eric Swalwell in a sexual misconduct investigation. Russia struck Kyiv overnight, killing at least 17 and targeting critical infrastructure for the first time in months.
author: GoCheckMyNews
key_fact: Israel moved from denial to confirmed responsibility to criminal investigation into a child's killing; federal law enforcement escalated probes into a former congressman and an alleged ISIS sympathizer; and Russia resumed targeting of Ukrainian civilian infrastructure amid winter vulnerability.
bottom_line: Israel moved from denial to confirmed responsibility and criminal investigation into a child's death; the FBI escalated criminal probes into former congressman Swalwell and alleged ISIS sympathizer Bowie; and Russia resumed targeting of Kyiv's critical infrastructure as Ukrainian defenses face resupply delays. Watch the scope and timeline of Israel's criminal investigation and whether it produces indictments; the federal court filings in Swalwell's case and any defense challenges to investigative methods; and whether Ukraine's explicit call for accelerated Patriot interceptor delivery affects Western resupply timelines.
body: The evening's reporting captures three separate escalations in official accountability and enforcement. Israel's confirmation that its military fired on the car carrying Hind Rajab in 2024 and its announcement of a criminal investigation reversed years of denials about the five-year-old's death. Rajab was killed along with six relatives; an ambulance sent to retrieve her was shelled, killing two paramedics, Yusuf al-Zeino and Ahmed al-Madhoun. The Hind Rajab Foundation expressed no confidence in the investigation, signaling skepticism about the military's internal review process. What remains open is whether the investigation results in criminal charges or convictions of individual soldiers.

In the United States, federal law enforcement expanded two separate criminal investigations. The FBI seized an iPhone and MacBook Pro from former Democratic Rep. Eric Swalwell during search warrant executions Saturday at San Francisco International Airport and Sunday at his Washington, D.C. residence. The seizures mark an escalation from the House Ethics Committee inquiry that culminated in Swalwell's resignation in April. Investigators are examining potential charges under a federal statute making it a crime for officials to deprive individuals of constitutional rights. On the same day, Jessica Bowie, 35, of Albany, New York, was apprehended as she obtained what she believed to be an explosive device with the intent of deploying it at the New York State Capitol to kill public officials. She faces charges of attempting to provide material support to ISIS. The government's case rests on confidential sources, surveillance, and undercover investigation.

Overseas, Russia resumed purposeful targeting of critical infrastructure in Kyiv for the first time in several months. A drone and missile attack around midnight killed at least 17 people and injured more than 40, striking a children's hospital, school, apartment blocks, and warehouses. The Ukrainian Air Force indicated that none of the Russian ballistic missiles were intercepted. Power was cut to thousands of properties; the mayor warned of disrupted hot water supply in multiple districts. The strike compounds Ukraine's winter vulnerability as Russia targets heat and power systems while Ukrainian air defenses face replenishment delays from Western suppliers.

On banking supervision, the Federal Reserve issued a Written Agreement with SouthPoint Bancshares dated August 14, 2026, and terminated a Cease and Desist Order against Deutsche Bank AG that had been in effect since April 2017. The reporting establishes the enforcement action but does not disclose the underlying supervisory concerns or corrective measures required of SouthPoint.
